title: minimize-capture-noise-and-synchronized-replay-for-shared-kernel-batches
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Problem: Interleaved multi-stream decodes occasionally produce nondeterministic outcomes after CUDA graph capture and replay. The root causes observed in postmortems are: transient kernel launch ordering differences, KL cache alignment mismatches across prefill windows, and attention-fusion heuristics choosing different kernels under capture vs live execution. These divergence modes increase tail latency and have caused two customer incidents (INC-2026-03A, INC-2026-03B).

Goal: Reduce capture-induced nondeterminism ('capture noise') to near-zero for supported model families on dedicated nodes by synchronizing kernel selection and introducing a capture-stable kernel policy, while keeping p99 latency and throughput within 5% of current baseline. Implement safe fallbacks that detect replay divergence and route to a verified non-cuda-graph path without request loss.

Scope: Platform runtime (graph capture + replay), kernel selection policy, prefill/decode scheduling alignment, and a small number of guardrails in the request router. Does NOT include model-level re-training or quantization changes.
proposal_summary: 1) Introduce a deterministic kernel policy for capture sessions: a serialization of kernel-choice decisions based on captured request attributes (model family, seq len, quantization level, prefill-window-hash). 2) During capture, record a compact 'capture manifest' with kernel selectors and kv-cache epoch checksum; persist in the graph metadata. 3) On replay, verify manifest; if mismatch above a safe threshold, trigger 'graceful degrade' to non-cuda-graph decode for that request or cohort, and emit detailed telemetry. 4) Add prefill window aligner to scheduler to avoid partial-window captures: coalesce small prefill batches into canonical window sizes before capture. 5) Harden attention-fusion heuristics by adding an 'is-capture' mode that disables speculative fusion rules that are non-deterministic across driver/firmware versions. 6) CI: add fuzz-replay harness and a replay-scan nightly that replays recent graphs against a golden executor to detect drift.
acceptance_criteria: Single-node nightly replay-scan shows <0.05% divergence rate across 10k sampled captures for resizable families (e.g., Llama2-13B, MPT-7B)
Automated fault-injection (kernel-probe) test triggers graceful degrade path without dropped requests and with correct output verification
P99 latency for multi-stream baseline test runs within 5% of current production numbers on dedicated GPU pools
Capture manifests are emitted for every captured graph and available in the Console (per-graph metadata)
test_plan: Unit: deterministic-kernel-policy tests covering all branch permutations
Integration: capture -> replay loop on multi-stream harness with random interleaving (10k iterations)
Staging: enable capture-manifest + replay-verifier on 10% of dedicated pool; monitor divergence and latency impacts for 48h
Canary: route 1% of production traffic to new capture-stable path for one customer cohort; collect metrics and error budgets
rollout_plan: Phase 1: merge kernel policy + capture manifest, enable in staging with replay-scan. Phase 2: gating: 'is-capture' heuristics toggled by runtime flag; run canary 1% traffic -> monitor 72h. Phase 3: enable scheduler prefill-alignment on dedicated pools; run customer canaries for model families. Phase 4: full enable with automatic fallback after 2026-03-28 if metrics stable.
notes: Trade-offs: deterministic kernel policy increases memory for manifest metadata (~0.5-1KB/graph) and may disable some speculative fusion optimizations; acceptable given reliability targets.
Performance: microbenchmarks show ~1.8% throughput regression in worst-case for some MHA kernels when forcing 'capture-stable' variants; plan to optimize hot-path kernels next sprint.
Security/Compliance: capture manifests do not contain customer prompt text; only fingerprinted attributes and checksums. Security review flagged and approved by Priya Kothari on 2026-03-09.
Follow-ups: investigate automatic manifest-based graph compaction (ENG-413002) and cross-node manifest reconciliation for multi-GPU graphs (ENG-413100).
